html:
The Russia-Ukraine conflict intensified today with a deadly strike on buses in Kramatorsk, killing at least 30, as Moscow expands its targeting of Ukraine’s transport system and UN figures show a surge in civilian fatalities this year compared to 2025. This escalation coincides with preparations for peace discussions in Miami, where Trump envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are set to present new proposals to Ukrainian negotiators and European officials.

Russia-Ukraine: Beyond the Kramatorsk attack, Russia’s expanded targeting of Ukraine’s transport system includes trains and ports, further paralyzing the network and endangering civilians. Blackouts have worsened in Kyiv, while Black Sea security remains precarious after suspected Russian drone attacks hit Turkish-owned cargo ships in EU waters, with one sinking off Bulgaria. Separately, military representatives from all 32 NATO member states convened in Kyiv.

US-Iran Tensions: Tensions remain elevated between the US and Iran, with Trump stating there would be no attack on Iran before the US elections and that "productive" talks are ongoing, while also affirming Iran will not possess nuclear weapons. Simultaneously, the US imposed fresh sanctions on 17 vessels of Iran’s 'shadow fleet'. An IRGC advisor declared the Strait of Hormuz closed and under Iranian control until Iran’s demands are met, a claim rejected by US CentCom, which stated 20 million barrels of crude are moving through the strait. Separately, Iran’s President Pezeshkian met with Putin in Turkmenistan, where they stressed strengthening strategic ties, and Putin told Pezeshkian he would "do everything" to help end the Middle East war.

Middle East Security: Houthi attacks continue to destabilize the Arabian Peninsula, with three people killed and 36 injured in strikes on Saudi Arabia's Abha and Riyadh airports. Yemen's military spokesperson claimed a ballistic missile strike on King Khalid Airport disrupted operations, leading airlines to cancel flights. The Saudi-led coalition vowed these attacks "will not go unpunished," and Pakistan confirmed the deployment of its forces to Saudi Arabia under the Mecca pact. Elsewhere, an Israeli army report stated one soldier was killed and three wounded in southern Lebanon amidst Israeli artillery fire in the area.

European Domestic Affairs: Spain faces growing social unrest over a housing crisis, with protesters blaming 'vulture funds' and hundreds camping in Madrid. The Spanish prime minister has called a snap election, following mass protests sparked by the death of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal, whose eviction had become a "cause celebre." Concurrently, France is experiencing widespread student protests demanding better education and less police brutality, with demonstrations across the country and over 500 detentions, an unrest that appears to be spreading to Belgium.

East Asia Developments: South Korea announced it would recall its ambassador to Ukraine, escalating a diplomatic spat after Kyiv disclosed the transfer of North Korean prisoners of war to Seoul. This comes as South Korea successfully test-flew its first domestically developed hypersonic weapon, following a recent North Korean test, and amid increased tensions after land mine explosions near the border, which North Korea denies responsibility for.
